# Cooldown behaviour documentation

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

Update all affected documentation so the model-cooldown contract, the
cheap-switch gate and the bounded wake are discoverable and unambiguous, and so
the withdrawn client-drain constraint is recorded where a future change would
see it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC7 — Documentation: all related documentation is updated to reflect the cooldown changes, including code comments and the herdr README.
- [ ] The on-disk cooldown contract (file, schemaVersion, fields, tolerance) is documented in one place with cross-references from both consuming packages.
- [ ] The fail-closed direction (an unreadable signal means no cheap switch) and the bounded default are documented as explicit behaviour.
- [ ] The withdrawn client-drain constraint is recorded so a future change cannot silently regress it.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (planning tooling extracts only the first line of each
bullet).

- AC7 (parent AC7 "Documentation"): covers code comments, the herdr README, the
  mode-switch design doc and the downtime-dispatcher dev doc — one section per
  surface, each pointing at the shared contract module rather than restating the
  field list.
- Single source of truth: the shared module header describes the fields and
  tolerance rules; the other documents link to it.
- Fail-closed and bounded default: state the direction explicitly (unreadable ⇒
  hold fast; absent ⇒ normal decision) and the clamp values.
- Regression guard: a short "must not regress" note citing the withdrawn
  predecessor records the constraint next to the behaviour it constrains.

## Deliverables

- Updated code comments in both packages.
- Updated `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` and
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- Updated `packages/herdr/README.md`.
- Cross-references from every surface to the single contract of record.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/README.md`
- `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts`

## Dependencies

Depends on `Recovery loop records durable cooldown`, `Cheap-switch gate honours
model cooldowns`, `Bounded wake of one cooled-down job` and `Bounded default
cooldown and fail-closed hardening`.

# Cooldown regression guard and full-suite verification

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

Prove the withdrawn client-side drain has not been reintroduced and that the
whole project suite passes with the cooldown changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC6 — Tests: unit + integration tests cover detection, gating, wake, cross-root and failure paths.
- [ ] AC8 — Full-suite: the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] Regression guard: a regression test proves the withdrawn client drain is not reintroduced.
- [ ] Baseline: the suite test count and runtime before and after are recorded in a work-item comment.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (planning tooling extracts only the first line of each
bullet).

- AC6 (parent AC6 "Tests"): the covered paths are detection (exhaustion
  classification), gating (cheap-switch hold), wake (bounded resume),
  cross-root (two-root integration) and the failure paths (unreadable signal,
  unwritable marker, absent Retry-After).
- AC8 (parent AC8 "Full-suite"): run the project suite command from the
  repository root and require a clean pass.
- Regression guard specifics: assert there is no client-side slot-count
  completion gate, no dispatch pause and no unbounded latch in the new paths —
  the three things the withdrawn predecessor
  (`WL-0MUWIHUL2000JEFR`) removed.
- Baseline: record the pre-change and post-change totals so suite drift is
  visible.

## Deliverables

- The regression test proving the withdrawn drain is not reintroduced.
- A recorded full-suite run (count and runtime before/after).
- The baseline comment on the parent work item.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-loop.test.ts`
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`

## Dependencies

Depends on `Recovery loop records durable cooldown`, `Cheap-switch gate honours
model cooldowns`, `Bounded wake of one cooled-down job` and `Bounded default
cooldown and fail-closed hardening`.
data.title: Cooldown regression guard and full-suite verification

data.description:
Automated guard that the watch/refresh path never blocks the TUI event loop (parent WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN).

## Scope
- Extend `packages/herdr/src/hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` (precedent WL-0MUY1CZES0099A04 / WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P) to exercise the watch-triggered refresh path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- An automated regression test asserts pane keyboard input stays responsive during and after a watch-triggered refresh (≤ 100 ms p95 input lag), and fails if the watch/refresh path blocks the TUI event loop.
- The test is deterministic and runs in the standard suite, using bounded timeouts / stdio isolation as per the precedent.

## Dependencies
- F3 wiring.
data.title: Input responsiveness regression guard

discovered-from:WL-0MV563ADO008FT6H

When the worktree cannot fast-forward the main checkout's dev and the push is rejected as non-fast-forward, implement.py finish's rebase-and-retry path raises an unhandled NameError:

  ERROR: Unhandled exception: name 'cwd' is not defined
  INFO: Safety reset: WL-0MV563ADO008FT6H status in-progress -> open

Observed on 2026-10-12 finishing WL-0MV563ADO008FT6H. The worktree was removed and the item reset to open even though the commit existed; recovery required manually re-adding the worktree, rebasing onto origin/dev, rebuilding (dist/ is gitignored and is not recreated when a worktree is re-added), re-running the full suite and pushing.

Expected: the push-recovery path should rebase-and-retry without an unhandled NameError, or fail with an actionable message that leaves the commit/worktree recoverable.

File: ~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py (the branch that logs 'Push failed (non-fast-forward); attempting rebase and retry ...').
